For employment, OR 328b and statutory record duties (OR 958f, ArGV 1 73, AHVV 143, DBG 126) are the main justification.
rules.verification: DSG Art. 31 read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: None noted.

rules.scope: Disclosure of employee data abroad (e.g. hosting, sub-processors, AI providers).
rules.summary: Data may go abroad where the Federal Council has found adequate protection (DSV Annex 1, which lists e.g. EU states and the USA for organisations certified under the Swiss-US Data Privacy Framework); otherwise appropriate safeguards (treaty, data protection clauses notified to FDPIC, etc.) or Art. 17 exceptions (explicit consent, contract with the data subject).
rules.verification: DSG Art. 16-17 and DSV (SR 235.11, consolidation 2025-12-01) Art. 8 / Annex 1 read on Fedlex filestore. DSV Annex 1 USA entry: 'Für Personendaten, die von Organisationen bearbeitet werden, die gemäss den Grundsätzen des Datenschutzrahmens zwischen der Schweiz und den USA zertifiziert sind, gilt ein angemessenes Schutzniveau als gewährleistet'.
rules.limitations: Annex 1 can change; recheck before relying on it.

rules.scope: Automated individual decisions (relevant to AI features).
rules.summary: Controller must inform the data subject of a decision based solely on automated processing that has a legal effect or significantly affects them. An AI assistant must not make HR decisions automatically.
rules.verification: DSG Art. 21 para. 1 read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: None noted.

rules.scope: Personnel dossier content and access (EDÖB guidance).
rules.summary: Dossier may only hold data indispensable to perform the contract; must be sorted regularly; data processed only by HR; access must be documented and traceable; illness information falls under medical secrecy; generally no disclosure to third parties without consent.
rules.verification: Fetched EDÖB page (WebFetch). Other quotes on the page: 'Dieses Dossier darf nur die Daten enthalten, die für die Abwicklung des Arbeitsvertrags unerlässlich sind.'; 'Die Daten aus den Dossiers dürfen nur von der Personalabteilung bearbeitet werden'.
rules.limitations: Guidance, not statute.

rules.scope: Form of retention of business books and vouchers (incl. electronic payroll records).
rules.summary: Records may be kept on unalterable media, or on alterable media if integrity is ensured by technical means (e.g. digital signatures), storage time is provably fixed (timestamps), etc.; media must be checked regularly; migrations allowed if completeness, accuracy, availability and readability are kept, and must be logged with the log retained with the data.
rules.verification: GeBüV (SR 221.431) Art. 9-10 read on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2013-01-01, latest available).
rules.limitations: S3 Object Lock / hash chains likely satisfy integrity, but conformity is a legal/audit judgement.

rules.scope: Employment for an indefinite period or more than one month.
rules.summary: Employer must inform the employee in writing within one month of start about parties, start date, function, wage and supplements, weekly working time; changes within one month after taking effect.
rules.verification: OR Art. 330b read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: Full list of items truncated in excerpt.

rules.scope: All employers paying cash wages.
rules.summary: Employee must receive a written pay statement (schriftliche Abrechnung) with each wage payment; this part (Art. 323b para. 1 second sentence) is relatively mandatory (OR 362). Module may store the externally produced payslip; it does not compute it.
rules.verification: OR Art. 323b and 362 read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: OR does not prescribe payslip content; content comes from practice and social-insurance/tax needs.

rules.scope: Employers under the Labour Act.
rules.summary: Registers must contain all data needed to enforce the ArG, incl. personal details, type of employment, entry and exit, daily and weekly working time incl. compensatory and overtime, breaks of 30 minutes or more, etc. Must be available to enforcement bodies. Art. 73a (waiver via GAV for autonomous staff above an income threshold, list kept available to authorities) and Art. 73b (simplified recording by agreement) allow reduced recording.
rules.verification: ArGV 1 Art. 73, 73a, 73b read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: Time tracking itself is out of V1 scope; storing imported time records is in scope.

rules.scope: All employers (AHV/IV/EO).
rules.summary: Employers deduct the employee contribution from every wage, verify registration data against official ID papers, settle periodically with the compensation fund and provide data for individual accounts; settle wages within 30 days after the settlement period (AHVV 36); the annual wage declaration is due by 30 January after the contribution year (leaflet 2.01).
rules.verification: AHVG Art. 51 and AHVV Art. 36 ('Die Arbeitgeber haben die Löhne innert 30 Tagen nach Ablauf der Abrechnungsperiode abzurechnen.') read on Fedlex filestore; leaflet 2.01 (ahv-iv.ch/p/2.01.d, 2026 edition) text extracted from the PDF: 'Diese Lohndeklaration muss spätestens bis zum 30. Januar nach Ende des Beitragsjahres bei der Ausgleichskasse eingereicht werden.'
rules.limitations: V1 stores results only; contribution rates not researched (on purpose). BVG, UVG, ALV, FAK not researched.

rules.scope: Employer audits by compensation funds.
rules.summary: Periodic employer audits (Art. 68b AHVG) normally on site, or remotely with electronic access; audit covers all documents needed and the non-time-barred contribution period. Obstructing it, e.g. by lacking records under Art. 143 para. 2, has cost consequences (Art. 164 area).
rules.verification: AHVV Art. 162-163 read on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2026-01-01).
rules.limitations: Exact article for the cost consequence of obstructing the audit only partly read.

rules.scope: ATSG Art. 46 (record keeping).
rules.summary: ATSG Art. 46 obliges the insurance carrier (Versicherungsträger), not the employer, to record all relevant documents systematically. It is not an employer retention rule.
rules.verification: ATSG (SR 830.1, consolidation 2024-01-01) read on Fedlex filestore.
rules.limitations: None.

rules.scope: All employers: salary certificate (Lohnausweis, ESTV form 11).
rules.summary: Employers must issue written certificates of their payments to employees (DBG 127 para. 1 let. a); ESTV provides form 11 and the Wegleitung (versions for tax periods from 2025 and from 2026, published 15 Jan 2026). V1 can store the externally produced Lohnausweis but does not generate it.
rules.verification: DBG Art. 127 read on Fedlex filestore; ESTV page https://www.estv.admin.ch/de/lohnausweis-rentenbescheinigung fetched: 'Arbeitgebende bescheinigen ihren Arbeitnehmenden die erbrachten Leistungen mit dem entsprechenden Formular.'
rules.limitations: Wegleitung PDF itself not read; cantonal duties to send certificates directly to tax authorities (some cantons) not researched.

rules.scope: Employers of source-taxed employees (foreign nationals without settlement permit resident in CH, DBG 83; non-resident workers incl. frontier workers, DBG 91).
rules.summary: Employer withholds source tax, issues a statement of the deduction to the employee, settles periodically with the competent (cantonal) authority and grants insight into all documents; deduction applies even if the worker lives in another canton; employer is liable. ESTV computes the federal share; tariffs are cantonal. Automatic calculation is blocked in V1.
rules.verification: DBG Art. 83, 85, 88, 89, 91 read on Fedlex filestore; Art. 88 wording in force since 1 Jan 2021 per footnote.
rules.limitations: Per-canton tariffs, thresholds for subsequent ordinary assessment (EFD amount) and cantonal procedures not researched.

rules.scope: Employers of source-taxed employees.
rules.summary: Employers must report the hiring of source-taxed persons to the competent tax authority within eight days of the start of work on the prescribed form (or via monthly electronic settlement); employees must report changes relevant to source tax.
rules.verification: QStV (SR 642.118.2) Art. 5 read on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2025-01-10).
rules.limitations: The QStV has no explicit retention period; see CH-RET-QST-001.

rules.scope: Cantonal execution of source tax (example: Canton of Zurich).
rules.summary: Source tax is settled directly with the entitled canton under its own rules; tariffs are canton-dependent and readable tariffs are only on cantonal websites (ESTV). Zurich example: monthly, quarterly if fewer than ten source-taxed employees, data per employee and month, filing within 30 days after the period, channels eQuest, ELM (Swissdec), paper, simplified procedure; corrections until 31 March of the following year.
rules.verification: Fetched Zurich page and ESTV page https://www.estv.admin.ch/de/quellensteuer ('Der Tarif für die Quellensteuer ist kantonsabhängig und kann daher über die kantonalen Steuerverwaltungen abgefragt werden.'). Only 1 of 26 cantons checked.
rules.limitations: A zh.ch business-portal page reportedly gives a different deadline (10th of the following month) per a search summary; not fetched. Other 25 cantons not researched.

rules.scope: VAT (MWSTG, SR 641.20).
rules.summary: Not relevant to payroll records: wages are not VAT supplies. MWSTG Art. 70 only governs VAT-liable persons' books (retention until absolute limitation of the VAT claim, OR 958f reserved). No VAT logic needed in the Employees module.
rules.verification: MWSTG Art. 70 read on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2025-03-31). The statement that wages are outside VAT is general reasoning, not a fetched excerpt.
rules.limitations: Fringe benefits/staff supplies can have VAT effects; out of scope.

rules.scope: Employers of foreign nationals.
rules.summary: Before the foreign national starts work, the employer must verify the work authorisation by inspecting the permit or enquiring with the authorities. Module should record permit type, expiry and the check date; a document copy is not legally required (not found).
rules.verification: AIG Art. 91 read on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2026-11-01).
rules.limitations: SEM page/directives not fetched (404); sanctions (AIG 117, 122) not read.

rules.scope: Frontier workers (Grenzgänger) and other non-resident employees.
rules.summary: Non-resident workers are subject to source tax on Swiss employment income (DBG 91); special rules per neighbour-state agreement (e.g. QStV Art. 1 para. 2: source tax of frontier workers under para. 1 let. n-r is 80% of the normal tariff; QStV Art. 8 federal share for frontier workers from Germany; Art. 5a certificate for France residents). Frontier workers hold a special permit card (VZAE).
rules.verification: DBG Art. 91 and QStV Art. 1, 5a, 8, 14-15 headings/text read on Fedlex filestore; QStV excerpt: 'Die Quellensteuer der Grenzgängerinnen und Grenzgänger nach Absatz 1 Buchstaben n–r beträgt 80 Prozent der Quellensteuer nach dem Tarifcode, für den sie die Voraussetzungen erfüllen.'
rules.limitations: Which letters n-r cover which agreements (CH-IT etc.) not read in detail; DTAs not researched.

rules.scope: Social security of cross-border employees (EU/EFTA).
rules.summary: Under the CH-EU Agreement on Free Movement of Persons (SR 0.142.112.681, Annex II) Switzerland applies Regulations (EC) 883/2004 and 987/2009; in principle only one state is competent. Frontier workers with a Swiss employer teleworking 25%-49.9% from DE, AT, FR, IT (from 2024-01-01) or LI can stay insured in Switzerland with an A1 certificate requested via ALPS.
rules.verification: Fetched BSV pages sozialversicherungsabkommen and telearbeit (WebFetch); FZA Annex II on Fedlex filestore (consolidation 2020-12-15) lists 'Verordnung (EG) Nr. 883/2004 des Europäischen Parlaments und des Rates vom 29. April 2004 zur Koordinierung der Systeme der sozialen Sicherheit'.
rules.limitations: Telework quote from https://www.bsv.admin.ch/de/telearbeit: 'Die Vereinbarung gilt für grenzüberschreitende Telearbeit zwischen 25 % und 49,9 % der Gesamtarbeitszeit.' The FZA consolidation found is dated 2020-12-15; newer Annex II amendments may exist.

rules.scope: Wage tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax, social security contributions
rules.summary: Not offered in V1. German payroll requires ELStAM retrieval, per-Land church tax, contribution group keys and Einzugsstelle per employee (BVV § 8 Abs. 1 Nr. 13-15) and per-period records; these are produced by certified external payroll software and imported as results.
rules.verification: read BVV § 8
rules.limitations: None; deliberately out of scope.

rules.scope: Processing of employee and applicant data (applicants and former employees count as employees)
rules.summary: Employee data may be processed where necessary for hiring, performing or ending employment. Consent is judged in light of the employee's dependency; it is voluntary mainly where the employee gains an advantage or interests align; must be written or electronic. Special categories allowed where necessary for employment/social-security law obligations. Following CJEU C-34/21 (30.03.2023) national rules that do not meet Art. 88(2) GDPR must be disregarded unless they are a valid Art. 6(3) basis; § 26 Abs. 1 BDSG is worded like the Hessian rule at issue, so rely on GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)/(c) and Art. 9(2)(b) directly.
rules.verification: BDSG § 26 read on gesetze-im-internet.de (no amendment note); C-34/21 operative part read on EUR-Lex (CELEX 62021CJ0034); curia.europa.eu redirect did not render
rules.limitations: Whether § 26 Abs. 1 BDSG still applies after C-34/21 is contested; no German court ruling was fetched. The C-34/21 case concerned § 23 HDSIG (Hesse).

rules.scope: Church-tax data (ELStAM)
rules.summary: ELStAM provided to the employer includes church-tax deduction features, derived from legal membership in a tax-levying religious community; religion is a GDPR Art. 9 special category. ELStAM may be used without consent only to withhold wage and church tax. Helvetly should not store the religion/church-tax feature unless the external payroll export requires it, and never expose it beyond payroll roles.
rules.verification: read EStG § 39e Abs. 2-3 and § 39 Abs. 8 on gesetze-im-internet.de
rules.limitations: Church tax rate per Land not verified; do not hard-code.

rules.scope: Written statement of essential terms
rules.summary: Employer must record essential terms, sign and hand them over (items 1, 7, 8 by first working day; 2-6, 9, 10 by 7th day; rest within one month). Text form with electronic transmission is allowed if the employee can access, save and print it and confirms receipt; not allowed in § 2a SchwarzArbG sectors; 'elektronische Form' (qualified e-signature) is excluded.
rules.verification: read NachwG § 2 on gesetze-im-internet.de
rules.limitations: Helvetly e-signature is not a substitute where written form is required; flag sector exclusion.

rules.scope: All employers
rules.summary: BAG 1 ABR 22/21 (13.09.2022): employers must introduce a system able to record employees' working time (§ 3 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 ArbSchG, read with CJEU C-55/18). No statutory form or retention period for these general records was found.
rules.verification: read BAG press release on bundesarbeitsgericht.de
rules.limitations: A planned ArbZG amendment on electronic time recording was not researched.

rules.scope: Businesses with a works council
rules.summary: Introducing and using technical systems designed to monitor employee behaviour or performance is subject to works council co-determination. An HR tool with time records or activity logs can fall under this.
rules.verification: read § 87 BetrVG on gesetze-im-internet.de
rules.limitations: Information for the customer; Helvetly cannot enforce it.

rules.scope: Employee data in Austria
rules.summary: GDPR applies directly; DSG grants a fundamental right to secrecy of personal data and a data-secrecy duty (Datengeheimnis, § 6 DSG) for controller, processor and their staff. No general Austrian employee-data statute was found; the DSB considers employee consent as a rule unsuitable in the employment context (stated for video surveillance).
rules.verification: DSG consolidated text read on RIS (Fassung 15.11.2026); DSB consent statement only seen in a search snippet of https://dsb.gv.at/faqs/foto-video, page not fetched
rules.limitations: DSB FAQ not fetched directly.

rules.scope: Payroll filings and payments
rules.summary: Annual Lohnzettel (L16) for all employees, electronically by end of February of the following year (paper by 31 January); monthly contribution statement to ÖGK by the 15th of the following month; wage taxes to the tax office, Kommunalsteuer to the municipality and contributions to ÖGK by the 15th. Not offered in V1 (no ELDA/FinanzOnline submission).
rules.verification: usp.gv.at, Letzte Aktualisierung 1. Januar 2026 (BMF)
rules.limitations: Deadlines shown for information only; not tracked as reminders in V1.

rules.scope: Businesses with a works council
rules.summary: Introducing systems that automatically process employee data beyond general personal data and qualifications needs works council consent (or a Schlichtungsstelle decision), unless use stays within duties from law, collective norms or the contract.
rules.verification: read ArbVG § 96a on RIS
rules.limitations: Information for the customer.

rules.scope: Workers posted or hired out to Austria
rules.summary: Contract/Dienstzettel, payslips or payment proofs, working-time records and wage classification documents must be kept available in German or English at the work site (or electronically accessible) for the duration of employment in Austria / the posting.
rules.verification: read LSD-BG § 22 on RIS
rules.limitations: Edge case for V1.

rules.scope: Personnel management files
rules.summary: Only staff in charge of personnel management may consult employee data; line managers only what they need; actions by authorised persons should be logged; staff representatives informed before use; employees informed of controller, purpose, retention, legal basis (legal obligation or legitimate interest).
rules.verification: Read CNIL page (17 août 2023).
rules.limitations: Soft law.

rules.scope: CNIL HR retention referential (soft law)
rules.summary: Distinguishes mandatory periods (blue) from CNIL-recommended ones (grey); HR file kept during employment, then intermediate archive only where legally required or for evidence, within the limitation period.
rules.verification: Downloaded PDF from cnil.fr and decoded text streams locally (Publié le 2 avril 2026, Mis à jour le 20 mai 2026).
rules.limitations: Text extraction from table layout may have lost words; quotes checked against decoded text.

rules.scope: Employers collecting income tax at source (prélèvement à la source)
rules.summary: Employer applies the rate transmitted electronically by DGFiP to wages; the rate is returned in a compte-rendu after each DSN; PAS is declared and paid via the monthly DSN. Helvetly V1 does not file DSN nor compute PAS.
rules.verification: Read BOFiP BOI-IR-PAS-30-10-20 and impots.gouv.fr 'Les modalités du prélèvement à la source' (modifié le 28/08/2023).
rules.limitations: PAS rate confidentiality: DGFiP supplies the rate only to the collector; Helvetly must not ask the employee for it beyond the imported payroll result.

rules.scope: Employers of foreign workers
rules.summary: Copy of each work authorisation annexed to the registre unique du personnel and accessible to CSE delegation and inspectors; register records the type and number of the title.
rules.verification: Read D1221-24 on legifrance.gouv.fr.
rules.limitations: D1221-23 content list seen only in search snippet.

rules.scope: IRPEF regional and municipal surcharges
rules.summary: Addizionale regionale base rate 1.23%, regions may vary within state limits; addizionale comunale up to 0.8% (exceptions); both depend on fiscal domicile on 1 January. Automatic calculation is not offered in V1.
rules.verification: Read finanze.gov.it pages for addizionale regionale and comunale ('L'addizionale è dovuta al comune nel quale il contribuente ha il domicilio fiscale alla data del 1° gennaio').
rules.limitations: Rates change yearly per region/comune.

rules.scope: Employers (Statuto dei lavoratori art. 8; Codice privacy art. 113)
rules.summary: Employer may not investigate political, religious or union opinions of the worker, nor facts irrelevant to professional aptitude, at hiring or during employment; Codice privacy art. 113 keeps this in force.
rules.verification: Read L. 300/1970 art. 8 and D.Lgs. 196/2003 art. 113 ('Resta fermo quanto disposto dall'articolo 8 della legge 20 maggio 1970, n. 300') on normattiva.it.

rules.scope: Remote monitoring tools (Statuto dei lavoratori art. 4)
rules.summary: Tools enabling remote monitoring only for organisational/production needs, safety or asset protection, with union agreement or INL authorisation; not required for work tools and attendance recorders; collected data usable for employment purposes only with adequate information to the worker and in compliance with D.Lgs. 196/2003. Relevant if an AI assistant analyses employee activity.
rules.verification: Read art. 4 on normattiva.it (Testo in vigore dal 8-10-2016).

rules.scope: Private employers except domestic
rules.summary: LUL must record for each worker name, codice fiscale, qualification/level, base pay, seniority, insurance positions, all cash/in-kind payments, deductions, tax deductions, and a daily attendance calendar; entries completed for each month by the end of the following month; fines for omitted/unfaithful entries and for failure to keep it.
rules.verification: Read art. 39 on normattiva.it.
rules.limitations: Helvetly's payroll register import is NOT a legally kept LUL; the LUL remains the consultant's/payroll provider's responsibility.

rules.scope: Data an employer may request (Kodeks pracy art. 22[1])
rules.summary: Candidate: name, birth date, contact data, education, qualifications, employment history (no pay history); employee additionally: address, PESEL (or ID document type/number), family data where needed for special rights, education/history if not given before, bank account number unless cash payment requested.
rules.verification: read consolidated Kodeks pracy (obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu 1 Sept 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1245) fetched as PDF from api.sejm.gov.pl (official Sejm ELI API) and text-extracted
rules.limitations: Items in § 3 pkt 4-5 summarised from the act; check full list before shipping the form.

rules.scope: Consent limits (Kodeks pracy art. 22[1a], 22[1b])
rules.summary: Consent may cover other data except GDPR Art. 10 (criminal) data; refusal/withdrawal must cause no detriment; Art. 9 special-category data only if supplied on the employee's initiative.
rules.verification: read consolidated Kodeks pracy (obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu 1 Sept 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1245) fetched as PDF from api.sejm.gov.pl (official Sejm ELI API) and text-extracted
rules.limitations: No consent-based collection of criminal-record data; special categories only on employee initiative.

rules.scope: UODO employer guide (2018, marked archival; update under consultation)
rules.summary: Employer may not demand data beyond what the law specifies, especially data unrelated to employment.
rules.verification: read UODO PDF 'Ochrona danych osobowych w miejscu pracy. Poradnik dla pracodawców' (Oct 2018)
rules.limitations: Guide predates 2019 KP changes and is marked archival.

rules.scope: Personnel file structure (rozporządzenie w sprawie dokumentacji pracowniczej)
rules.summary: Akta osobowe consist of 5 parts: A recruitment and pre-employment medical; B establishment and course of employment (contract, scope of duties, acknowledgements…); C termination; D disciplinary/order liability; E sobriety/drug control (summary).
rules.verification: read consolidated rozporządzenie (obwieszczenie MRPiPS 23 March 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 474) via api.sejm.gov.pl
rules.limitations: Only parts A and B text checked verbatim; contents of C, D, E taken from the same paragraph structure but not quoted.

rules.scope: Electronic documentation (Kodeks pracy art. 94 pkt 9a, art. 94[8])
rules.summary: Documentation may be kept on paper or electronically; form may be changed (paper→electronic by scan signed with qualified e-seal/e-signature).
rules.verification: read consolidated Kodeks pracy (obwieszczenie Marszałka Sejmu 1 Sept 2026, Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1245) fetched as PDF from api.sejm.gov.pl (official Sejm ELI API) and text-extracted
rules.limitations: The brief cited art. 94[5] for e-documentation; in the 2026 text art. 94[5] is about re-hire, electronic form changes are art. 94[8].

rules.scope: BSN processing
rules.summary: Organisations outside government may use the BSN only where a law provides; employers do so for wage tax (URLB art. 7.9 requires the BSN on the data statement).
rules.verification: read AP BSN page (HTTP 200 via curl; WebFetch returned 403)
rules.limitations: Do not use the BSN as an internal employee key or show it outside payroll contexts.

rules.scope: AP: personnel file retention guidance
rules.summary: Data without a statutory period: generally 2 years after the employee leaves; earlier deletion if no longer needed; payroll data and contracts 7 years; ID copy and loonbelastingverklaring 5 years.
rules.verification: read AP page 'Personeelsdossiers' (HTTP 200)
rules.limitations: Guidance, not statute; disputes justify longer retention (per AP, not quoted).

rules.scope: Wage tax records (Wet LB 1964 art. 28 lid 1)
rules.summary: Withholding employer must collect data from employee, keep a loonadministratie, establish identity and record type, number and copy of ID (and of residence/work permit for non-exempt foreign workers) in the loonadministratie.
rules.verification: read Wet LB 1964 art. 28 on wetten.overheid.nl (geldend van 08-10-2026)

rules.scope: IRPF withholding
rules.summary: IRPF applies across Spain without prejudice to the foral systems of the Basque Country (concierto) and Navarre (convenio); the regional part uses the scale approved by each autonomous community. Automatic calculation is not offered in V1.
rules.verification: Read Ley 35/2006 arts. 4 and 74 via BOE open-data API.

rules.scope: Blocking instead of immediate deletion (legal hold)
rules.summary: When rectification or erasure is due, the controller must block the data: identify and reserve it with technical/organisational measures preventing processing, including viewing, except for courts, prosecutors and competent authorities, only for the limitation period of possible liabilities; then destroy. Blocked data may not be used for any other purpose.
rules.verification: Read LOPDGDD art. 32 via BOE open-data API (fecha_vigencia 20181207).
rules.limitations: Product implication: an 'erase' action during a legal-hold period should switch the record to a blocked state hidden from normal users, not hard-delete.

rules.scope: Digital rights at work (LOPDGDD arts. 87-91)
rules.summary: Workers' privacy in employer-provided digital devices (87), right to digital disconnection (88), limits on video/audio surveillance (89), geolocation with prior information (90); collective agreements may add guarantees (91).
rules.verification: Read arts. 87-91 via BOE open-data API.

rules.scope: Employee records
rules.summary: No data protection time limits; set a retention schedule listing record types, uses and retention period.
rules.verification: read ICO guidance 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: ICO notes guidance under review after the Data (Use and Access) Act.

rules.scope: Special category employee data
rules.summary: Special category data needs a lawful basis plus a condition; the employment condition (DPA 2018 Sch.1 Pt 1 para 1) covers legal employment/social security obligations, not purely contractual ones, and needs an appropriate policy document.
rules.verification: read revised text on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-15 and ICO guidance
rules.limitations: Helvetly cannot hold the employer's appropriate policy document; flag it to the user.

rules.scope: All PAYE employers
rules.summary: Payroll must be reported to HMRC via a Full Payment Submission on or before payday; EPS by the 19th of the following tax month to claim reductions. Helvetly V1 does not file RTI; the external payroll software does.
rules.verification: read guidance page on gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: RTI filing not offered in V1.

rules.scope: Imported payroll results
rules.summary: Imported payroll results (pay, deductions, tax code, SSP/SMP) are PAYE records; keep them at least 3 years after the end of the tax year (6 years where they prove NMW compliance).
rules.verification: read revised text on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Import must keep tax year and pay reference period to compute retention.

rules.scope: Payroll record content
rules.summary: HMRC lists records to keep: pay, deductions, reports and payments to HMRC, leave and sickness absences, tax code notices, taxable expenses or benefits, Payroll Giving documents.
rules.verification: read guidance page on gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Non-exhaustive guidance.

rules.scope: Employers hiring in the UK
rules.summary: Right to work copies must be clear, unalterable copies (whole document; specified passport pages) and the check date retained; from 1.10.2026 facial recognition for manual checks must come from an RtW DVSP (art. 6(1A)).
rules.verification: read revised text on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Store originals as immutable files; Home Office guide PDF not read.

rules.scope: Employees resident in Scotland
rules.summary: Scottish Income Tax depends on where the employee lives, not where the employer is; employed taxpayers get a tax code starting with 'S'. V1 does not calculate tax; store the tax code from the external payroll.
rules.verification: read guidance page on gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Rates not collected (V1 has no calculation).

rules.scope: Employees resident in Wales
rules.summary: Welsh rates apply to people living in Wales (longest-residence test if moving); HMRC prefixes the tax code with 'C'.
rules.verification: read guidance page on gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Rates not collected.

rules.scope: Transfers of UK employee data abroad
rules.summary: Transfers to EEA states, Gibraltar and (for data provided in Switzerland) Switzerland, Guernsey, Isle of Man, Jersey, Andorra and others are treated as approved under DPA 2018 Sch.21 paras 4-5 (as amended by DUAA 2025 from 5.2.2026).
rules.verification: read revised text on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-15
rules.limitations: Exact scope of the Switzerland entry ('personal data provided in Switzerland') should be confirmed by counsel for UK-to-CH transfers; separate UK adequacy regulations for other countries not listed here.

rules.scope: Federal, state and local withholding and contributions
rules.summary: Calculation depends on federal tables (Pub. 15-T, not researched), per-state income tax (none in TX/FL/WA), state UI/SUI employer rates (e.g. CA new-employer UI 3.4% and ETT 0.1% on first $7,000 per EDD search result, not fetched), employee-paid state programs (CA SDI 1.3% 2026 per EDD search result; NY PFL 0.432% 2026 per search result; WA PFML 1.13% 2026 per search result) and local resident taxes (NYC, Yonkers 16.75% of NYS tax per NYS-50). Rates change yearly. Automatic calculation is blocked in V1.
rules.verification: Only the Yonkers surcharge and NYC withholding scope read on NYS-50; other rates seen only in search summaries and NOT verified - do not encode them.
rules.limitations: No rate may be used from this fragment except as an explanation of why automation is blocked.

rules.scope: Multi-state and local taxes
rules.summary: NY resident tax: all wages paid to NYC residents are subject to NYC withholding regardless of work location; nonresidents working partly in NY need allocation records (IT-2104.1). Each employee needs a work state and residence locality. General work-state vs. residence and reciprocity rules for other states were not researched.
rules.limitations: Reciprocity agreements, remote-work convenience rules, and other states' locals not researched.

rules.scope: Medical and genetic information about employees
rules.summary: ADA: medical information from exams/inquiries must be collected and kept on separate forms in separate medical files, treated as confidential (limited disclosure to supervisors for accommodations, first aid, investigators). GINA: genetic information likewise in separate medical files. FMLA medical certifications kept as confidential medical records separate from personnel files.
rules.verification: Read eCFR 29 CFR 1630.14, 1635.9(a)(1), 825.500(g) via renderer API.
rules.limitations: Helvetly must keep a separate 'medical' document category with its own access list, excluded from the general personnel file and from AI.

rules.scope: EEO-1 Component 1
rules.summary: Annual EEO-1 filing applies only to private employers with 100+ employees and federal contractors with 50+ (plus conditions). Not offered in V1.
rules.verification: Read EEOC page.
rules.limitations: Demographic data (race/ethnicity, sex) is sensitive; not collected in V1.

rules.scope: Helvetly V1 register of payroll results computed elsewhere
rules.summary: Federal employment-tax records must include amounts and dates of wage payments, names, addresses, SSNs, occupations, dates of employment, deposits and copies of returns. A register imported from an external payroll provider can hold these as data; the employer remains responsible for completeness and IRS availability.
rules.verification: Read IRS page.
rules.limitations: Records must be 'available for IRS review'; export capability needed.

rules.scope: FLSA non-exempt employees
rules.summary: Required payroll data: full name and SSN, address, birth date if under 19, sex and occupation, workweek start, hours each day and week, pay basis, regular rate, straight-time and overtime earnings, additions/deductions, total wages per period, pay date and period covered. Records may be kept at the worksite or a central office.
rules.verification: Read DOL WHD Fact Sheet #21.
rules.limitations: 29 CFR 516.2 text itself not separately read.

rules.scope: Form I-9 document copies
rules.summary: Copying I-9 documents is optional (except E-Verify alternative remote examination); if done for non-E-Verify reasons it must be done for all employees; copies are kept with the I-9 or employee record and do not replace the form.
rules.verification: Read USCIS M-274 section 10.2.
rules.limitations: E-Verify participants using alternative remote examination must keep copies.

rules.scope: California state payroll taxes
rules.summary: UI and ETT are employer contributions; SDI and PIT are withheld from employees' wages and reported to EDD. Not offered in V1.
rules.verification: Read EDD page.
rules.limitations: Filing forms and due dates not researched.

rules.scope: CCPA/CPRA businesses (gross revenue >= $26.625M adjusted 2025, or 100,000+ CA consumers/households, or 50%+ revenue from selling/sharing)
rules.summary: Since the workforce exemption expired on 2022-12-31, CCPA rights cover California employees and job applicants of covered businesses.
rules.verification: Read CPPA FAQ on cppa.ca.gov.
rules.limitations: Most small Helvetly customers fall below thresholds; specific employee rights (access, deletion, correction, sensitive PI limits) not detailed here.

rules.scope: California itemized wage statement (Lab. Code 226(a))
rules.summary: Each payment needs a statement with gross wages, total hours (not for salaried exempt), piece units/rates, all deductions, net wages, inclusive pay-period dates, employee name and SSN identifier, legal entity name and address, all hourly rates and hours at each. Records available within 21 calendar days of request.
rules.verification: Read DLSE paydays FAQ (appears older, cites 2003); statute text blocked (403).
rules.limitations: Current statutory list (e.g. SSN truncation, sick leave balance) not verified.

rules.scope: NY Paid Family Leave
rules.summary: Covered employers must provide statutory PFL benefits through an insurance policy (usually a rider on the disability policy) or self-insurance; employees fund it through a payroll deduction, or the employer may pay.
rules.verification: Read paidfamilyleave.ny.gov.
rules.limitations: NY disability benefits (DBL) rules not researched.

rules.scope: New York wage statement (Lab. Law 195(3)) and hiring notice (195(1))
rules.summary: A statement must accompany every payment of wages (dates covered, employee and employer names, rates, gross wages, deductions, allowances, net wages; regular/overtime rates and hours for non-exempt). A wage notice in English and the employee's primary language is due at hiring, with signed acknowledgment.
rules.verification: Read nysenate.gov.
rules.limitations: Helvetly stores imported statements; it does not generate compliant statements in V1.

rules.scope: State income tax withholding
rules.summary: Texas has no personal income tax, so no state income tax withholding applies; state unemployment tax (TWC) still applies.
rules.verification: Read Texas Comptroller Fiscal Notes (Feb 2016). Constitution Art. 8 s. 24-a page did not render.
rules.limitations: Source is a 2016 article; constitutional text not read.

rules.scope: State income tax on natural persons
rules.summary: Florida Constitution limits any tax on income of resident natural persons to amounts creditable against federal or other-state tax; in practice no state wage withholding. Reemployment tax applies; workers do not pay it and employers must not deduct it.
rules.verification: Read Florida Constitution Art. VII s. 5(a) on flsenate.gov (fetch summary); 'no withholding' is an inference.
rules.limitations: Florida minimum wage (Art. X s. 24) contains no record-retention period (checked); the assumed 3-year rule in the brief does not exist there.

rules.scope: State income tax and payroll premiums
rules.summary: Washington currently has no individual income tax; DOR announces a new tax (SB 6346) from 2028-01-01 on AGI over $1 million. Employers of all sizes must collect Paid Family & Medical Leave premiums (or pay on employees' behalf) and file quarterly reports with hours and wages, even with no payroll; WA Cares premiums are employee-paid.
rules.verification: Read DOR income tax page and paidleave.wa.gov employer responsibilities page ('Every quarter, all employers must complete and file a report and pay Paid Leave premiums').
rules.limitations: No PFML-specific retention period was found; SB 6346 withholding mechanics unknown.

rules.scope: Personopplysningsloven § 1
rules.summary: GDPR applies as Norwegian law with EEA adaptations.
rules.verification: read personopplysningsloven (LOV-2018-06-15-38) § 1 on lovdata.no
rules.limitations: § 6 (special categories in employment) exists but its text was not reviewed.

rules.scope: Datenschutzgesetz (DSG) LGBl. 2018 Nr. 272 Art. 1
rules.summary: DSG implements Regulation (EU) 2016/679 in Liechtenstein.
rules.verification: read DSG text on gesetze.li (Lilex) via curl
rules.limitations: Employment-specific provisions not reviewed.

rules.scope: EEA EFTA states (NO, IS, LI)
rules.summary: GDPR incorporated into the EEA Agreement (Annex XI point 5e) by EEA Joint Committee Decision No 154/2018 of 6 July 2018.
rules.verification: read Decision 2018/1022 on EUR-Lex (OJ L 183, 19.7.2018); status 'In force'
rules.limitations: Exact entry-into-force date not shown on page (depends on Art. 103 notifications).

rules.scope: All controllers processing employee data in EU/EEA
rules.summary: Storage limitation: identifiable data kept no longer than necessary.
rules.verification: read GDPR on EUR-Lex (OJ text), Art. 5(1)(e)
rules.limitations: Purpose-specific periods come from national law.

rules.scope: Lawful bases for employee data
rules.summary: Employee data normally rests on contract (Art. 6(1)(b)), legal obligation (6(1)(c)) or legitimate interests (6(1)(f)).
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 6(1)(b),(c),(f) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: Legitimate interests requires a documented balancing test.

rules.scope: Consent in employment
rules.summary: Consent is presumed not freely given where it is a condition of a contract (Art. 7(4)); Recital 43: consent not valid where there is a clear imbalance; EDPB: employers should not rely on employee consent for most processing.
rules.verification: read EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 v1.1 (adopted 4 May 2020) para. 21 from the official PDF; GDPR Art. 7(4) and Recital 43 on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: Text extracted from PDF (spacing restored).

rules.scope: Data processing at work (WP29 Opinion 2/2017, WP249, adopted 8 June 2017)
rules.summary: Consent is highly unlikely to be a legal basis at work unless employees can refuse without adverse consequence; processing must be necessary, proportionate and transparent.
rules.verification: fetched WP249 PDF via ec.europa.eu Article 29 newsroom (document 45631); text extraction dropped short words, so only a contiguous fragment is quoted
rules.limitations: EDPB endorsement of WP249 was not confirmed from an EDPB page (endorsement URL returned 404).

rules.scope: Special categories in employment
rules.summary: Art. 9 data may be processed where necessary for employment, social security and social protection law obligations/rights authorised by law or collective agreement.
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 9(2)(b) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: Needs a Member State/collective-agreement legal basis; do not store health/union/religion data by default.

rules.scope: Criminal convictions data
rules.summary: Only under official authority or where authorised by Union/Member State law.
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 10 on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: Criminal-record certificates only where a national law requires them (e.g. PL KP art. 22[1a] excludes Art. 10 data from consent).

rules.scope: Erasure exceptions (legal hold)
rules.summary: Right to erasure does not apply where processing is needed to comply with a legal obligation or for legal claims; Art. 18(1)(c) lets the data subject require restriction for their legal claims.
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 17(3)(b),(e) and 18(1)(c) on EUR-Lex

rules.scope: Automated decisions
rules.summary: Right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects.
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 22(1) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: An AI assistant must not make employment decisions; human review required.

rules.scope: DPIA
rules.summary: DPIA required before processing likely to result in a high risk (e.g. systematic monitoring, AI over employee data).
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 35(1) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: National DPIA lists not checked.

rules.scope: Transfers outside EU/EEA
rules.summary: Transfers only under Chapter V: adequacy (Art. 45), appropriate safeguards (Art. 46) or derogations (Art. 49).
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 44, 46(1), 49(1) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: Hosting/sub-processor locations must be checked by the operator.

rules.scope: Employment-specific national rules (Art. 88)
rules.summary: Member States may adopt more specific rules on employee data by law or collective agreement, with suitable safeguards for dignity, transparency, intra-group transfers and monitoring.
rules.verification: read GDPR Art. 88(1),(2) on EUR-Lex
rules.limitations: National rules must be checked per country.

rules.scope: CJEU C-34/21 Hauptpersonalrat (30 March 2023)
rules.summary: National 'more specific rules' must meet Art. 88(2); provisions that do not must be disregarded unless they are a valid Art. 6(3) legal basis.
rules.verification: read judgment C-34/21 on EUR-Lex (operative part)

rules.scope: Directive (EU) 2019/1152 transparent working conditions
rules.summary: Employer must give written information on essential aspects (parties, place, role, start, pay, working time, leave, notice, collective agreements, social security institutions); core items within 7 calendar days from the first working day, rest within one month; electronic form allowed if accessible, storable, printable with proof of transmission.
rules.verification: read Directive 2019/1152 on EUR-Lex, Art. 3, 4, 5, 21
rules.limitations: Transposition deadline 1 Aug 2022; national transpositions (PL KP art. 29 § 3, NL BW 7:655) not verified here.

rules.scope: Applicable social security legislation (Reg. 883/2004)
rules.summary: One Member State's legislation only; normally the state where work is done; posting up to 24 months keeps home-state legislation; work in two or more states: residence state if a substantial part is done there, otherwise rules in Art. 13(1)(b).
rules.verification: read consolidated Reg. 883/2004 (version 31.07.2019) on EUR-Lex, Art. 11-13
rules.limitations: Applies to EEA states and CH via agreements (not verified here). The app must not determine applicable legislation automatically.

rules.scope: Substantial activity (25%) and A1 attestation (Reg. 987/2009)
rules.summary: Substantial part = quantitatively substantial share; for employees working time and/or remuneration; under 25% indicates no substantial part. The competent institution issues on request an attestation that its legislation applies (portable document A1).
rules.verification: read Reg. 987/2009 (original OJ text) on EUR-Lex, Art. 14(8), 15(1), 19(2)
rules.limitations: Consolidated version URL returned 404; later amendments to these articles not checked. 'A1' name of the form is not in the article text.
